1: Chapter 1: A Visitor in the Rain
It had been raining on Pierrefeu for three days. In the spring, Claire Martin's elder sister had left for Paris, and since then Claire had been running the little village pharmacy on her own.
When night fell, she shut the shutters, counted the day's takings, blew out the lamp, and went upstairs.
She had barely lain down when someone pounded violently on the door downstairs. A man's voice called, "Is anyone there?"
On the doorstep stood a young man soaked to the bone, his left arm wrapped in a bloodstained cloth. He introduced himself: his name was Pierre Lapin, and he belonged to the Azure Dragon Society.
"You must treat me," Lapin said in a low voice. "I can pay. Three thousand five hundred francs — will that be enough?"
He pulled a letter wrapped in oilskin from his jacket. "This letter must reach the abbey of Saint-Vent before the eighteenth of May."
Since her sister had left, Claire had often felt low in the evenings, but that night she had no time to dwell on it.
Yet she refused his money and said only, "Tomorrow at dawn, I will take you up into the mountains."
2: At daybreak they set out. Claire carried a basket on her back containing bread, medicinal herbs, and an old umbrella.

Halfway up the slope, they met old Gaston Roux, who was splitting wood. He set down his axe and told them in a low voice that the evening before, three strangers had been questioning people at the entrance to the village about a wounded young man.
"Take the footpath, my little Claire," said Gaston Roux. "The main road isn't safe." Claire thanked him.
The path was narrow and slippery. Claire walked ahead, placing each step with confidence. Lapin followed her without a word.
At noon the rain stopped; the mist slowly lifted, and the roof of the abbey of Saint-Vent appeared in the distance. A nun stood at the door — Sister Agnès, whose duty it was to welcome visitors.
Sister Agnès took the letter, examined the red seal, and nodded. "The abbess has been waiting for this letter for 2 years."
Lapin said to Claire, "I owe you my life." Claire smiled. "Then next time, fix the roof of my pharmacy." Lapin stayed at the abbey.
That evening, Claire came back down the mountain alone. By the time she reached home, it was already dark; she lit the lamp and sat for a long while behind the counter.
